However, we stated that we believe proposing to unconditionally package payment for CY 2027 for SaMS technologies that are currently conditionally packaged under the OPPS may have resulted in interruptions to patient access. Given that we intended for this policy to be a first step towards more comprehensive payment policy changes and sought to minimize disruption, we believed it was more appropriate to propose to maintain the clinical APC and status indicator assignments for these codes. Therefore, for CY 2027, we proposed to maintain the clinical APC and status indicator assignments for SaMS that are currently conditionally packaged under the OPPS.
Similarly, there are other HCPCS codes that describe SaMS assigned to status indicator “E1” (Items, codes, and services not covered by any Medicare outpatient benefit category; statutorily excluded; not reasonable and necessary), status indicator “N” (Items or services packaged into APC rates), or status indicator “M” (Items and services not billable to the FI or MAC). Since these are not separately paid services under the OPPS for CY 2026, for CY 2027, we proposed to maintain the OPPS status indicators to which they are currently assigned.
We provided a table with the various SaMS HCPCS codes that were impacted by our proposals. Table 83 provides the proposed CY 2027 APC and status indicator assignments for codes we proposed to designate as SaMS services and that are currently assigned to clinical APCs or are not separately paid under the OPPS for CY 2026. We referred readers to section III.C. of the proposed rule for a discussion on the proposed CY 2027 payment rates for SaMS codes that are currently assigned to new technology APCs for CY 2026. In addition, we referred readers to Addendum B of the proposed rule for proposed CY 2027 OPPS payment rates and status indicators for HCPCS codes that we proposed to designate as SaMS. We requested comment on our proposals, including the list of HCPCS codes we proposed to designate as SaMS and that we proposed to reassign to new technology APCs for CY 2027, including whether there were any additional HCPCS codes we should consider.
We received public comments on these proposals. The following is a summary of the comments we received and our responses.
Comment: Several commenters supported the proposed terminology change from SaaS to SaMS. One commenter explained that the proposed terminology would clarify the distinction between clinical algorithms and generic cloud tooling. A commenter requested that we clarify whether the transition to SaMS is intended solely as a naming convention or whether it reflects broader distinctions regarding the scope, classification, valuation or payment treatment of these technologies.
Response: We thank the commenters for their support. The terminology change from SaaS to SaMS seeks to clarify, as one commenter explained, the distinction between clinical algorithms used to furnish these services and generic cloud tooling.
Based on the comments received, for CY 2027, we are finalizing our proposal to change the terminology for these algorithm-based software services that are paid under Medicare from “SaaS” to “SaMS.”
Comment: Many commenters requested clarification regarding the types of services that would be considered SaMS for purposes of this policy. For example, commenters asked whether remote care delivery or non-device clinical decision support (CDS) would be considered SaMS for purposes of separate payment. Similarly, we received comments regarding how CMS will distinguish separately paid software that supports clinical decision making from software that provides broader operational, administrative, or business functions. One commenter specifically requested that we expand our scope of services that we designate as SaMS to include those that perform analyses on structured clinical data conforming to recognized interoperability standards such that super intelligence-enabled comprehensive clinical trial eligibility analysis would be payable under the OPPS.[173]
Response: We thank the commenters for their interest in better understanding the scope of our policy. Regarding whether we would consider remote care delivery services as SaMS for purposes of this policy, we refer the commenter to our proposal where we specified that SaMS is separate from RPM and RTM, which are digital health tools for remotely tracking patient data. Furthermore, software that includes broader operational, administrative, or business functions, including clinical trial eligibility analysis, would not be considered SaMS under current policy. These kinds of software services can provide operational efficiencies but would not have a Medicare benefit category to allow for separate payment under OPPS.
We also appreciate commenters' input regarding whether CMS would consider non-device CDS as SaMS. The 36 services that we proposed to designate as SaMS, and that we previously referred to as SaaS, are regulated by the FDA as devices and therefore would not be considered non-device CDS. We note that although SaMS described in this section of this final rule with comment period (section X.B.1.), are required to have FDA marketing authorization to receive Medicare payment, “SaMS analyses performed on laboratory tests,” which are described in the following section of this final rule with comment period (section X.B.2.), currently do not require FDA marketing authorization in order to receive payment. As the CY ( printed page 70614) 2027 SaMS policy is an interim policy that seeks to maintain payment for CY 2027, we are declining to expand the scope of our policy to include non-device CDS at this time, although we note that there are existing non-device CDS services assigned to clinical APCs for CY 2026. We will consider expanding and further clarifying the scope of the SaMS policy for future rulemaking.
Comment: We received several comments requesting information on CMS's process for identifying the 36 proposed HCPCS codes to be designated as SaMS. Commenters requested that we adopt, in the future, specific criteria that CMS will use to determine whether a service is payable as a SaMS under OPPS. For example, a commenter requested that we include the definitions and criteria from the recently updated Appendix S, effective June 2026, available via the AMA's website to identify SaMS codes. Other commenters requested that we identify SaMS codes based on functionality rather than input modality. We also received comments requesting that CMS align its clinical or diagnostic functionality criteria with the definitions that are used by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for their review of indications for use and device descriptions in their guidance documents and clearance processes.
Response: We appreciate the comments. To identify the 36 proposed SaMS CPT codes, we examined all CPT codes currently paid under the OPPS to determine which codes aligned with the SaMS terminology provided in the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule, specifically “software-based technologies that support clinical decision making through algorithmic analysis, including those that provide clinical or diagnostic functionality” as a framework. We excluded RTM, RPM, non-device CDS, and services that we did not believe would fall under a Medicare benefit category, including those that are administrative in function. For instance, software that serves as the infrastructure that the provider uses to furnish another separately paid service.
Given the interim nature of the proposed policy, we will take the criteria concerns raised by the commenters, including establishing specific criteria for SaMS service for purposes of payment under the OPPS, into consideration for future rulemaking. We welcome public engagement from interested parties on these issues, including whether there are services that should be designated as SaMS in the future.
Comment: We received a significant number of comments and requests from various interested parties regarding the proposed APC and status indicator assignments for certain SaMS services. Some of the requests included services that we did not identify as SaMS for the proposed rule and interested parties requested that they be added to the SaMS list. Others requested to maintain the clinical APC assignments for specific services we identified as SaMS versus assigning them to new technology APCs. A third category of requests included services that we identified as SaMS and assigned to new technology APCs, but interested parties requested different new technology APC assignments. We also received several comments requesting for certain services to be designated as SaMS and assigned to status indicator “O1” for CY 2027. A summary of the SaMS APC Specific requests and our responses are below.
We also note that since the CY 2027 proposed rule was published, the AMA revised their `release and effective date' calendar for new category III CPT codes. The new category III CPT codes that were going to be effective January 1, 2027, became effective October 1, 2026. New category III CPT codes with January 1, 2027, effective dates that we had designated as SaMS for the proposed rule, were assigned to clinical APCs and status indicators for the October 2026 update.
We received several comments requesting for certain services to be designated as SaMS and assigned to status indicator “O1” for CY 2027.
a. Biomechanical Computed Tomography (BCT) Analysis, CPT Code 0554T
Biomechanical Computed Tomography (BCT) analysis involves the use of a previous CT scan that is used by a computer software program to measure both the bone strength and bone mineral density of the hip or spine region. These services are described by CPT codes 0554T, 0555T, 0556T, 0557T, 0558T, and 0743T. CPT code 0554T is currently assigned to status indicator `M' (Items and Services Not Billable to the MAC. Not paid under OPPS). We received public comment on this service.
Comment: A commenter requested we designate CPT code 0554T (Bone strength and fracture risk using finite element analysis of functional data and bone-mineral density utilizing data from a computed tomography scan; retrieval and transmission of the scan data, assessment of bone strength and fracture risk and bone-mineral density, interpretation and report) as a SaMS. The commenter stated that since the other BCT codes (0555T, 0556T, 0557T, 0558T, 0743T) were designated as SaMS, it may be appropriate to designate CPT code 0554T as SaMS, although the commenter noted that the payment for CPT code 0554T is the sum of the payment for CPT codes 0555T-0557T.
Response: We thank the commenter for their input. For CPT code 0554T, we note that the current payment assignment is `M'. As we conveyed in the proposed rule, this interim payment policy is a step toward a more standardized approach that reduces payment rate variation across similar technologies. We believe that it is important to either maintain current payment rates ( i.e., by maintaining a service's new technology APC assignment) or assign new technology APCs that are closely aligned with current CY 2026 payment rates. We believe that because CPT code 0554T is not payable under OPPS, we should maintain the current status indicator. We are finalizing the status indicator assignment for CPT code 0554T as proposed. Please refer to Addendum B to this final rule with comment period, which is available on the CMS website, for the final CY 2027 payment rates.
b. Cardiosense Solution, CPT Code 1036T
The Cardiosense Solution, which is composed the CardioTagTM wearable sensor and the PCWP Analysis SoftwareTM, estimates a patient's pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) noninvasively to aid providers in the management of heart failure. CPT code 1036T ( Noninvasive hemodynamic assessment with pulmonary pressures and ejection fraction when performed, including passive acquisition of acoustic and electrical signals, augmentative algorithmic analysis, and generation of a clinical report with review, interpretation, and clinical integration by a physician or other qualified health care professional) is currently assigned to status indicator `E1' (Not covered by any Medicare outpatient benefit category; Statutorily excluded by Medicare; Not reasonable and necessary; Not paid by Medicare when submitted on outpatient claims (any outpatient bill type)) and receives no payment under OPPS. We received public comment on this service.
Comment: A commenter indicated that the devices in this service have recently received FDA marketing authorization (510(k) clearance for the CardioTagTM and De Novo authorization for the PCPW Analysis SoftwareTM) and ( printed page 70615) requested that we designate CPT code 1036T as a SaMS. The commenter requested that we assign it to APC 1503 and status indicator O1 using the following CPT codes as possible crosswalks:
1104T—Noninvasive cardiopulmonary assessment, including quantitative parameters, respectively predictive of significant epicardial coronary artery disease, pulmonary hypertension, and/or elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure, derived by augmentative algorithmic analysis of orthogonal voltage gradient and photoplethysmography signals, with automated report;
0962T—Assistive algorithmic analysis of acoustic and electrocardiogram recording for detection of cardiac dysfunction (eg, reduced ejection fraction, cardiac murmurs, atrial fibrillation), with review and interpretation by a physician or other qualified health care professional;
0764T—Assistive algorithmic electrocardiogram risk-based assessment for cardiac dysfunction (eg, low-ejection fraction, pulmonary hypertension, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy); related to concurrently performed electrocardiogram (List separately in addition to code for primary procedure); and
0765T—Assistive algorithmic electrocardiogram risk-based assessment for cardiac dysfunction (eg, low-ejection fraction, pulmonary hypertension, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy); related to previously performed electrocardiogram.
Response: We thank the commenter for their input. We agree with the commenter that, since these products recently received FDA marketing authorization, CPT code 1036T should be designated as a SaMS and paid under this final policy, as it describes an augmentative algorithmic analysis. We note that although SaMS described in this section of this final rule with comment period (section X.B.1.), such as CPT code 1036T, are required to have FDA marketing authorization to receive Medicare payment, “SaMS analyses performed on laboratory tests,” which are described in the following section of this final rule with comment period (section X.B.2.), currently do not require FDA marketing authorization in order to receive payment. We also agree with the commenter's choice of crosswalk codes, particularly CPT code 1104T. In summary, we are finalizing CPT code 1036T to APC 1503 (New Technology—Level 3 ($101-$200)) with a payment rate of $150.50. See Table 83 for the list of services designated as SaMS and their CY 2027 payment assignments.
c. DeepView AI® System, CPT Code 0972T
The DeepView AI® System (DeepView) is a non-invasive medical imaging platform used to evaluate burn wounds and predict their healing potential. This service is described by CPT 0972T (Assistive algorithmic classification of burn healing (ie, healing or nonhealing) by noninvasive multispectral imaging, including system set-up and acquisition, selection, and transmission of images, with automated generation of report) and is currently assigned to status indicator `E1' (Not covered by any Medicare outpatient benefit category; Statutorily excluded by Medicare; Not reasonable and necessary; Not paid by Medicare when submitted on outpatient claims (any outpatient bill type)). We received public comment on this service.
Comment: A commenter has requested that we designate this service as a SaMS and reassign CPT 0972 to APC 1523 (New Technology—Level 23 ($2501-$3000)) with a payment rate of $2,750.50, noting that DeepView received De Novo marketing authorization in May of 2026.
Response: We thank the commenter for their input. We agree with the commenter that this service should no longer be assigned to status indicator `E1' as the device utilized for this service has received De Novo marketing authorization and agree that this service should be designated as a SaMS. We disagree, however, with the commenter regarding the APC assignment and payment rate requested. We note that the commenter requested an APC assignment with a payment rate of $2,750.50 stating that this would cover the cost of the software. After review of the service and input from our medical advisors, we believe CPT 0992T (Noninvasive assessment of cardiac risk derived from augmentative software analysis of perivascular fat without concurrent computed tomography (CT) scan of the heart, including patient-specific clinical factors, with interpretation and report by a physician or other qualified health care professional) is an appropriate crosswalk because both services are utilizing imaging data with their software to obtain additional information for the clinician. We are assigning CPT 0972T to APC 1504 (New Technology—Level 4 ($201-$300)) with a payment of $250.50 and a status indicator of `O1'. See Table 83 below for the list of services designated as SaMS and their final CY 2027 APC assignments.
d. CureMatch, CPT Code 0794T
CPT code 0794T ( Patient-specific, assistive, rules-based algorithm for ranking pharmaco-oncologic treatment options based on the patient's tumor-specific cancer marker information obtained from prior molecular pathology, immunohistochemical, or other pathology results which have been previously interpreted and reported separately) is currently assigned to APC 5733 (Level 3 Minor Procedures) and status indicator `S'. We received public comment on this code.
Comment: A commenter requested that we designate this service as a SaMS consistent with our request for comment on additional codes that should be designated as SaMS.
Response: We thank the commenter for their input. We note that this service is considered a non-device CDS, and as explained earlier in this section, we are declining to expand the scope of our policy to include non-device CDS.
